hook.text: Leave wine exposed to air and it turns to vinegar. Acetic acid bacteria convert alcohol to acetic acid—on purpose or by accident.

buildup.text: Acetobacter species need oxygen to work. That's why vinegar forms on wine surfaces exposed to air.

discovery.text: The mother of vinegar—a rubbery disc floating in the bottle—is a cellulose mat produced by the bacteria.

twist.text: Kombucha's SCOBY is a symbiotic culture of acetic acid bacteria and yeast. It makes tea tangy and slightly fizzy.

climax.text: Balsamic vinegar ages up to 25 years. Acetic acid bacteria slowly concentrate and transform grape must into liquid gold.

punchline.text: Wine's worst enemy is vinegar's best friend. Same bacteria, different perspective.

quiz.question: What is the 'mother of vinegar'?
options: A cellulose mat produced by acetic acid bacteria
